Summarize assessment plans with their uncertainty

Source: R/api-multivariate-dstudy-summary.R
summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study.Rd

Read G, Phi and measurement SEM together with their confidence intervals, methods and limitations. Ordinary summary(d) retains its coefficient-table return value. Request intervals explicitly, or reuse saved interval results.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_multivariate_d_study'
summary(
  object,
  intervals = FALSE,
  parm = c("G", "Phi", "RelativeSEM", "AbsoluteSEM"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study'
print(x, digits = NULL, row.names = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

A result from mfrm_d_study().

intervals

FALSE (default) returns the original coefficient table. TRUE calculates the selected intervals using confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study(). Alternatively supply a saved confint(d) result or a list of such results. Saved results may contain different metrics, methods, scores or reference plans, but must match this D-study's source, plans and score weights. GENOVA-adjusted results retain adjusted points alongside original-source population intervals, with separate IntervalEstimate and IntervalBasis. Saved intervals must match the component treatment too.

parm

Metrics to calculate when intervals = TRUE. The default includes "G", "Phi", "RelativeSEM" and "AbsoluteSEM". Select fewer metrics when only those answer your question, particularly for explicitly requested expensive profile methods.

...

With intervals = TRUE, arguments to confint(d), including the required assumption = "normal", score or composite, level, method, reference, draws and seed. The default methods and score selection are those of confint(d). Unsupported requests fail explicitly; no alternative method is selected after a failure. With saved results or intervals = FALSE, additional arguments are rejected. For printing, arguments are passed to the displayed tables.

x

An interval-aware summary returned by this method.

digits

Display precision passed to the printed tables; NULL uses R's current setting. Stored estimates are unchanged.

row.names

Logical; print table row names? Defaults to FALSE.

Value

With intervals = FALSE, the unchanged object$coefficients data frame. Otherwise a summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study list containing:

  • table: one row per returned plan, metric and method, with Interval identifying the entry in intervals. It retains all original interval columns, including point/interval status, qualifications and any separate REML or residual-contrast IntervalCenter. Columns not applicable to a method are NA.

  • intervals: the complete original interval objects, retaining notes, diagnostics, reference context and their existing plot() methods.

  • source_design, source_rows, design_grid, weights and component_diagnostics: the original design, score and review context.

  • notes: method qualifications and interpretation reminders. print() returns the same saved summary invisibly. For G/Phi with method = "delta", the table retains and prints the coefficient sampling SE, distinct from measurement SEM. For GENOVA-adjusted points it is named IntervalSE and describes the original estimator, not the adjusted point. Normal-reference bounds outside [0,1] are not clipped.

Details

The intervals describe uncertainty from the observed G-study in the population coefficient or SEM of a specified future complete plan. They do not represent data already collected under that future plan. G and Phi are dimensionless; SEM is in the selected score's units. A larger G/Phi or smaller SEM does not alone determine a worthwhile plan: consider the intended decision, score meaning and task/rater burden.

reference requests the existing paired plan-difference procedure for each metric. It does not subtract marginal interval endpoints. Positive G/Phi differences and negative SEM differences favor the comparison plan, conditional on the stated model. Individual-plan and difference results remain explicitly labeled if both are supplied as saved results.

Printing and reopening a saved summary do not calculate intervals or refit models. Printing separates the main estimates, method qualifications and rows with unavailable points/intervals or incomplete width formulas; table retains all statuses and diagnostics columns. A completed approximate interval is qualified by its method, not automatically labeled a failure. Save the complete summary with saveRDS() to retain its context; CSV export of table alone loses weights, notes and diagnostics. Use plot(s$intervals[[1]]) for its existing forest plot, or supply a suitable single-metric individual-plan result to plot(d, intervals = ...). A summary does not create simultaneous guarantees across metrics, scores or selected plans. Read each method's qualifications. Availability is not proof of model validity or accurate finite-sample coverage.

Choose the operation

print(d) displays the D-study and returns it invisibly; summary(d) returns its coefficient table. This opt-in summary collects intervals; confint(d) calculates one metric at a time with the same inference rules. Neither changes d. print(s) displays the saved summary without any estimation, and s$table is the data frame for subsetting or CSV export. Use plot(d) for planning curves and plot(s$intervals$Phi) for a saved interval forest. A summary list itself is not a new plotting input.

This page explains the interface and reading order. Mathematical constructions, design-specific assumptions, numerical diagnostics and references are in confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study().

See also

mfrm_d_study(), confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study(), plot.mfrm_multivariate_d_study(), plot.mfrm_dstudy_intervals()

Examples

# Published synthetic data, not empirical speech-contest records.
ratings <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr"))
g <- mfrm_g_study(ratings, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL)
d <- mfrm_d_study(g, data.frame(Tasks = c(6, 12)),
  weights = c(V = .5, W = .5))
# Compare dependability and measurement error under the normal-effects model.
s <- summary(d, intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal")
print(s, digits = 3)
#> Assessment plans with source-study uncertainty
#> Source G-study: Balanced multivariate ANOVA 
#> Observed level counts (not future replication): Person = 10, Task = 6 
#> Source rows: 60 used of 60 ; 0 explicitly omitted.
#> Future complete balanced plans; counts apply to every person and score.
#> Intervals assume independent normal random effects; the assumption is not tested.
#> Nominal confidence level(s): 0.95 
#> Means over common random tasks 
#> Composite weights (not normalized):
#>   V   W 
#> 0.5 0.5 
#>  Scenario Tasks      Kind     Score      Metric Estimate Lower Upper Level
#>         1     6 Composite Composite           G    0.663 0.187 0.903  0.95
#>         2    12 Composite Composite           G    0.797 0.315 0.949  0.95
#>         1     6 Composite Composite         Phi    0.621 0.145 0.878  0.95
#>         2    12 Composite Composite         Phi    0.766 0.254 0.935  0.95
#>         1     6 Composite Composite RelativeSEM    0.418 0.347 0.527  0.95
#>         2    12 Composite Composite RelativeSEM    0.296 0.245 0.373  0.95
#>         1     6 Composite Composite AbsoluteSEM    0.459 0.389 0.701  0.95
#>         2    12 Composite Composite AbsoluteSEM    0.324 0.275 0.495  0.95
#>  MethodCode
#>     exact_f
#>     exact_f
#>         gci
#>         gci
#>         mls
#>         mls
#>         mls
#>         mls
#> Methods and qualifications:
#>  MethodCode                              Method
#>     exact_f        Exact F under normal effects
#>         gci Generalized CI under normal effects
#>         mls             Chi-square SEM interval
#>         mls      Graybill-Wang MLS SEM interval
#>                                                        Validation
#>                                     Normal-model F confidence set
#>              Generalized interval; frequentist coverage not exact
#>  Exact normal-model interval for positive mean-square expectation
#>           MLS approximation; pointwise coverage is not guaranteed
#> G/Phi are dimensionless; SEM is in score units. Available describes calculation, not coverage.
#> For differences, positive G/Phi and negative SEM favor the comparison plan.
#> Method assumptions and limitations: $notes; complete saved results: $intervals.
# One row per plan for absolute dependability; the complete table is retained.
subset(s$table, Metric == "Phi",
  select = c(Tasks, Estimate, Lower, Upper, Status))
#>   Tasks  Estimate     Lower     Upper    Status
#> 3     6 0.6205514 0.1453685 0.8782785 Available
#> 4    12 0.7658521 0.2538371 0.9351952 Available
# Reuse an interval for a curve, with no interval calculation.
p <- plot(d, metric = "Phi", intervals = s$intervals$Phi, draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p, "notes")
#>           Type
#> 1     subtitle
#> 2      caption
#> 3  uncertainty
#> 4  uncertainty
#> 5  uncertainty
#> 6  uncertainty
#> 7  uncertainty
#> 8  uncertainty
#> 9  uncertainty
#> 10 uncertainty
#> 11 uncertainty
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Text
#> 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Future complete crossed designs | Saved coefficient intervals | Source-study uncertainty
#> 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Points are requested scenarios; lines are guides. 
#> 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Nominal 95% intervals; method: Generalized CI under normal effects.
#> 4                           Ribbons connect saved endpoints at requested counts; intermediate plans are not evaluated. Isolated intervals use vertical segments. Open points have no interval; gaps are not interpolated. Inspect unavailable_intervals and the saved interval objects for reasons and diagnostics.
#> 5                                               Ribbons do not establish simultaneous coverage across scores or metrics. Any joint coverage across plans depends on the interval method and its stated model; drawing a band adds no coverage guarantee. Interval overlap does not test a score or plan difference.
#> 6                                                                                                                                                                    Phi includes the random facet main effect in absolute error. Independent normal effects and a complete balanced one-facet source are required.
#> 7                                                                                                                                           This generalized confidence interval does not guarantee exact frequentist coverage. More pivotal draws reduce numerical error, not model uncertainty or coverage error.
#> 8                                                                                                                           The GCI truncates its pivotal numerator at zero, not the source variance estimates. PointStatus and Status describe separate outputs; a zero endpoint is not proof of zero uncertainty.
#> 9                                                                                                                              The monte_carlo attribute contains separate 95% numerical bands for the endpoints. Increase draws if these bands affect the intended decision; save the whole result with saveRDS().
#> 10                                                                                                          All future counts transform the same single-rating interval and use source degrees of freedom. Rows are dependent; overlap does not test a plan difference. These are not pass/fail accuracy intervals.
#> 11 Widths lost to floating-point resolution leave endpoints and their numerical bands unavailable. A base pivotal interval with lost resolution cannot supply difference bounds, including for identical plans. Diagnostic single-rating bounds remain in pivot; the sampled zero atom retains its separate status.
